errorCodes.meaning: No key record on this custodian carries the named `keyId`. See [category conventions](../../_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#1-family-error-codes).

A header member is well-formed against the schema but unusable — a JOSE-registered member whose value is not of the type RFC 7515 defines for it, or an `x5c` whose first certificate does not carry the named key's public key. See [category conventions](../../_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#1-family-error-codes).
The named key exists but cannot sign a JWS in its current state — its `status` is not `active`, or the custodian has bound it to a protocol other than JWS.
The named key's `keyType` has no JOSE signature algorithm this custodian implements. An `x25519` key always draws this code.
The `header` names a member the custodian sets or refuses itself — `alg`, `crit`, `b64`, `jwk`, `jku` or `x5u` — or one its policy refuses for this key.

The payload cannot be signed as given — `payloadBase64Url` is not the canonical unpadded base64url encoding of any byte string, or `payload` holds a value RFC 8785 cannot serialise exactly (a number outside IEEE 754 double precision, a lone surrogate).

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

Response.description: The success response to a keys/sign-jws request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/keys/sign-jws/0.1#response. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

alg.description: The JOSE algorithm the custodian chose from the key's type and wrote into the header: `EdDSA` for `ed25519`, `ES256` for `p256`, `ES256K` for a secp256k1 key, `ML-DSA-44` and `ML-DSA-65` for `mldsa44` and `mldsa65`. Externally owned, carried verbatim.

jws.description: The JWS in compact serialisation: BASE64URL(header) '.' BASE64URL(payload) '.' BASE64URL(signature), unpadded. For ECDSA the signature is the fixed-width `r || s` of RFC 7518 §3.4, not DER.

keyId.description: The key that produced the signature. Echoed so a response separated from its request is still attributable.

schema.description: A request for a compact JWS (RFC 7515) made with a key the custodian holds. The producer supplies the protected header members it wants and the payload; the custodian sets `alg` from the key, serialises both itself, and signs the JWS signing input with no framing of its own. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

header.description: Protected header members the producer wants in the JWS — `typ`, `kid`, `x5c`, `cty`, or a profile's own (swiyu's `profile_version`). Member names and values are JOSE's and the profile's, carried verbatim. The custodian adds `alg` itself and refuses `alg`, `crit`, `b64`, `jwk`, `jku` and `x5u` (see the specification's Conformance section). Absent means a header of `alg` alone.

keyId.description: Identifier of the key to sign with, as `keys/show` describes it. The key MUST be `active` and of a type with a JOSE signature algorithm.

payload.description: The JWS payload, as a JSON object — for an OpenID4VP request object or any other JWT, its claims set. The custodian serialises it (RFC 8785) and base64url-encodes the result. Exactly one of `payload` and `payloadBase64Url` is present.

payloadBase64Url.description: The JWS payload as bytes, for a payload that is not a JSON object, base64url-encoded without padding. The custodian uses this string as the payload segment unchanged, after checking it is the canonical encoding of the bytes it decodes to. Exactly one of `payload` and `payloadBase64Url` is present.

schema.title: Keys — Sign JWS — payload
